name: Microsoft Azure
tagline: Enterprise-grade PaaS web hosting via Azure App Service, with a free tier
description: Microsoft Azure App Service is enterprise cloud PaaS hosting for websites and web apps, with tiered pricing from a free plan to autoscaling Premium.
about: This entry covers Azure strictly as a website-hosting option — specifically Azure App Service, Microsoft's platform-as-a-service (PaaS) product for hosting web apps, REST APIs and mobile backends — and briefly Virtual Machines as a self-managed alternative. Azure itself is a vastly broader cloud platform spanning databases, AI, networking, identity and hundreds of other services; none of that is in scope here, only what's comparable to a traditional web host.

App Service pricing runs in tiers: a Free (F1) tier with 60 CPU minutes/day, 1GB RAM and 1GB storage — no custom domain or autoscaling, suitable only for testing a small app. Basic (B1, 1 vCPU/1.75GB RAM) starts around $13/month on Linux and supports a custom domain and SSL but only manual scaling. Standard (S1, same specs as B1) runs roughly $57/month and adds autoscaling, staging slots and daily backups. Premium v3 (P1v3, 2 vCPU/8GB RAM) runs roughly $110-125/month with more compute, faster autoscale and network isolation options. Isolated (App Service Environment) tiers exist above that for dedicated, VNet-isolated deployments.

As a self-managed alternative, Azure Virtual Machines let you run any web server stack yourself on general-purpose or burstable VM sizes, billed per second/minute of compute plus storage and bandwidth — closer to a traditional VPS than App Service's managed platform, but with none of App Service's built-in deployment slots, autoscale rules or managed patching.
policies: Azure's free tier for App Service (F1) doesn't expire on a trial clock — it's a permanently free, resource-capped SKU, separate from the broader Azure free account's $200 30-day credit and 12 months of other free services for new sign-ups. There is no blanket money-back guarantee on paid App Service usage; Azure bills for compute already consumed, and refund requests are handled case-by-case through Microsoft billing support rather than a published refund window.

Pricing above is standard pay-as-you-go and was accurate as of this review's publish date — Azure pricing varies by region, currency and purchase option (reserved instances/savings plans reduce it substantially), so confirm current rates on Azure's own pricing page before committing budget.
